```{r}
#| include: false
for (f in list.files("R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
clean_all <- nanoparquet::read_parquet("data/clean/outbreaks.parquet")
clean <- filter(clean_all, in_scope)
info <- freshness_info()
current <- current_season_info(info$as_of)
weekly <- weekly_counts(clean, current)
ranges <- bind_rows(baseline_range(weekly, "pre-pandemic", current),
                    baseline_range(weekly, "post-pandemic", current))
this_season <- filter(clean, season == current$season)
resp_this <- filter(this_season, outbreak_type == "Respiratory")
fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
tbl <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-sm"', ...)
```

```{r}
     icon = "hourglass-split", color = "light")
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox

list(value = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(resp_this$agent_mix_group == "unknown")),
     icon = "question-circle", color = "light")
```

## Row {height="190px"}

::: {.card title="New outbreaks per week, against two comparison ranges"}

Counts are of outbreaks as published (one per affected unit or ward), by
week of onset. Testing and reporting changed during the pandemic, so this
season is compared with **two separate ranges**, never a pooled one:
the **pre-pandemic** seasons (2016/17 to 2018/19, plus 2019/20 up to
early March 2020) and the **post-pandemic** seasons (2022/23 to 2025/26).
Since 2020 more outbreaks are declared per affected unit and far more
pathogens are identified, so the post-pandemic range is the fairer
comparison. The pre-pandemic range shows how far the baseline has
moved.

:::

## Row {height="1100px"}

### Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: Respiratory
girafe_dash(plot_current_vs_baseline(weekly, ranges, current, "Respiratory"), width = 12, height = 10)
```

```{r}
#| title: Enteric
girafe_dash(plot_current_vs_baseline(weekly, ranges, current, "Enteric"), width = 12, height = 10)
```

```{r}
#| title: Table
weekly |>
  filter(season == current$season) |>
  left_join(ranges |> select(week, setting, type, baseline, lo, hi) |>
              mutate(range = paste0(lo, "-", hi)) |>
              select(-lo, -hi) |>
              tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = baseline, values_from = range),
            by = c("week", "setting", "type")) |>
  transmute(`ISO week` = iso_week_of_season_week(week), Type = type, Setting = setting,
            `New outbreaks` = n, `Pre-pandemic range` = `pre-pandemic`,
            `Post-pandemic range` = `post-pandemic`) |>
  arrange(desc(`ISO week` >= 35), desc(`ISO week`), Type, Setting) |>
  tbl()
```

# Agents

## Row {height="190px"}

::: {.card title="Which pathogens are behind this season's respiratory outbreaks?"}

Each outbreak is counted once. An outbreak where more than one pathogen was
found is shown as **Multiple agents**. For per-pathogen totals that count
such outbreaks under every pathogen found, see the table. *Unknown* means
no agent was identified, often because testing was not done or was
negative, so it says as much about testing as about the virus.

:::

## Row {height="520px"}

### Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: This season, weekly
girafe_dash(plot_agent_mix_weekly(agent_mix_weekly(clean, current$season, current$season_week)),
            width = 10, height = 5)
```

```{r}
#| title: Every season
girafe_dash(plot_agent_mix_seasons(agent_mix_by_season(clean)), width = 10, height = 5.5)
```

```{r}
#| title: Table
grp <- names(AGENT_GROUPS)
clean |>
  filter(outbreak_type == "Respiratory") |>
  group_by(Season = season) |>
  summarise(Outbreaks = n(),
            across(all_of(paste0("agent_", grp)), sum),
            `Co-detections` = sum(co_detection)) |>
  rename_with(~ unname(AGENT_GROUPS[sub("^agent_", "", .x)]), starts_with("agent_")) |>
  arrange(desc(Season)) |>
  tbl(caption = "Respiratory outbreaks by pathogen. An outbreak with two pathogens is counted under both, so pathogen columns add up to more than the total.")
```

# Duration

## Row {height="210px"}

::: {.card title="How long do outbreaks last?"}

Time from onset until the outbreak was declared over, for outbreaks that
began in the post-pandemic seasons (2022/23 onward). Outbreaks still open
are included up to the data-as-of date and then **censored**
(Kaplan–Meier), so recent, still-running outbreaks do not make durations
look shorter. Duration reflects the rules for declaring an outbreak over
(a set period with no new cases) as well as transmission.

:::

```{r}
#| include: false
dur <- duration_data(clean)
resp_dur <- filter(dur, outbreak_type == "Respiratory")
ent_dur <- filter(dur, outbreak_type == "Enteric")
agent_cols <- AGENT_COLOURS[c("COVID-19", "Influenza", "RSV", "Rhinovirus/enterovirus",
                              "Other respiratory virus", "Unknown")]
```

## Row {height="520px"}

### Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: Respiratory, by setting
girafe_dash(plot_km(resp_dur, "setting", SETTING_COLOURS), width = 9, height = 5)
```

```{r}
#| title: Respiratory, by pathogen
girafe_dash(plot_km(filter(resp_dur, agent %in% names(agent_cols)) |> droplevels(), "agent", agent_cols),
            width = 9, height = 5)
```

```{r}
#| title: Enteric, by setting
girafe_dash(plot_km(ent_dur, "setting", SETTING_COLOURS), width = 9, height = 5)
```

```{r}
#| title: Table
bind_rows(
  km_medians(resp_dur, "setting") |> mutate(Type = "Respiratory", By = "Setting"),
  km_medians(filter(resp_dur, agent %in% names(agent_cols)) |> droplevels(), "agent") |>
    mutate(Type = "Respiratory", By = "Pathogen"),
  km_medians(ent_dur, "setting") |> mutate(Type = "Enteric", By = "Setting")
) |>
  transmute(Type, Group = group, Outbreaks = outbreaks, `Still open` = still_open,
            `Median days` = median_days,
            `95% CI` = sprintf("%g-%g", ci_low, ci_high)) |>
  tbl(caption = "Median duration from Kaplan-Meier estimates, post-pandemic seasons.")
```

# Facilities

```{r}
#| include: false
fsc <- facility_season_counts(clean)
# Complete seasons only: 2015/16 starts in January 2016 and the current
# season is still in progress, so both would understate repeat outbreaks.
complete_seasons <- season_label(2016:(current$season_start_year - 1L))
rs <- repeat_share(fsc) |> filter(season %in% complete_seasons) |>
  mutate(setting = factor(setting, levels = names(SETTING_COLOURS)))
last_complete <- season_label(current$season_start_year - 1L)
dist <- recurrence_distribution(fsc) |> filter(season == last_complete) |>
  mutate(setting = factor(setting, levels = rev(names(SETTING_COLOURS))))
```

## Row {height="210px"}

::: {.card title="Do the same facilities have repeat outbreaks?"}

A facility is a physical site (one address, split by setting where an
LTCH and a retirement home share an address). Counts are outbreaks as
published, so several wards affected at once count separately. Only
facilities with at least one outbreak appear; the dataset has no list of
all facilities, so facilities with none cannot be counted. Counts are not
adjusted for facility size, so individual facilities are deliberately not
ranked.

:::

## Row {height="520px"}

### Column {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: Repeat outbreaks by season
girafe_dash(plot_repeat_share(rs), width = 9, height = 5)
```

```{r}
#| title: !expr paste("Outbreaks per facility,", last_complete)
girafe_dash(plot_recurrence_distribution(dist), width = 12, height = 4.5)
```

```{r}
#| title: Table
rs |>
  transmute(Season = season, Setting = setting, `Facilities with outbreaks` = facilities,
            `With 2+ outbreaks` = repeat_facilities, Share = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * share_repeat)) |>
  arrange(desc(Season), Setting) |>
  tbl()
```

# About

::: {.card title="About this dashboard"}

An unofficial, independent surveillance summary built from the City of
Toronto's open dataset *Outbreaks in Toronto Healthcare Institutions*,
which Toronto Public Health refreshes every Thursday with data as of
Wednesday afternoon. It is updated automatically each week; the banner on
the first page shows how current the data are.

**What it counts.** Declared outbreaks in hospitals, long-term care homes
(LTCH) and retirement homes, by week of onset. The data contain no case
counts, attack rates or deaths, so everything here is outbreak-level.

**Main caveats.**
Outbreaks are recorded per unit or ward, not per facility.
Testing and reporting changed during the pandemic, so counts before and
after 2020 are not directly comparable.
Pathogen labels changed over the years and have been harmonized.
"Coronavirus" in the source means seasonal coronaviruses, not COVID-19.
Recent weeks are provisional because outbreaks are reported with a delay.
Counts reflect testing and reporting practices as well as disease activity.

Methods and every analytical decision are documented in the
[project repository](https://github.com/samielsabri/toronto_healthcare_institutions_outbreaks),
including the [decisions log](https://github.com/samielsabri/toronto_healthcare_institutions_outbreaks/blob/main/reports/decisions.md).

:::
